title: Extension by zero on the localizing categories
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and let $j\colon U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible coefficient ring of [sk-def-localizing-closure]: a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, or one of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite inside a fixed algebraic closure and $\mathcal O_E$ is its valuation ring. Regard these as condensed rings with their indicated topologies. Use the ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, and the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], for $T=U,X$.
Then extension by zero $j_!=D(j_!)$ maps $\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, preserves all small direct sums on the ambient derived categories, and restricts to an exact, sum-preserving functor
$$
\Loc(\Dctf(U,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda)).
$$
The localizing closures and their direct sums are taken in the ordinary ambient derived categories as in [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text:
For any of the stated coefficient rings, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] states that the module-object functor $j_!$ is exact and left adjoint to $j^*$. Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to this additive exact functor. It gives the ambient triangulated functor $J=D(j_!)$ on the unbounded derived categories. Exactness also gives, directly on a complex representative,
$$H^r(JK)=\ker(j_!d^r)/\operatorname{im}(j_!d^{r-1})\cong j_!(\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1})=j_!H^r(K).$$
Indeed $j_!$ preserves the kernels and cokernels defining the image and its quotient. Thus $J$ preserves any cohomological vanishing interval; this calculation applies even when $K$ is unbounded.

proof.text:
By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$, abelian sheafification exists and is strong symmetric monoidal. Thus its local equivalences are monoidal: if $a(f)$ is invertible then $a(f\otimes P)\cong a(f)\otimes a(P)$ is invertible for every presheaf $P$. The ring object $\Lambda_T$ in abelian sheaves is a sheaf of rings, and its internal module objects identify with sectionwise module sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] on a small model of $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, in the fixed sheaf-value universe, for $T=U,X$. For each internal module category, let $E_T$ be this equivalence to sectionwise modules. A colimit is obtained by applying a quasi-inverse of $E_T$ to the colimit of the image diagram: the equivalence of Hom sets verifies its universal property. Kernels and cokernels are identified by those same universal properties, so exactness of filtered colimits is inherited. A quasi-inverse image of a generator is a generator, since the fully faithful $E_T$ detects distinct maps. Thus both internal module categories are Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], both ambient derived categories have all small coproducts, computed by termwise coproducts of arbitrary representatives. The sheaf-level adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], applied to the small discrete indexing category $I$, give
$$j_!\Bigl(\bigoplus_{s\in I}K_s^r\Bigr)\cong\bigoplus_{s\in I}j_!K_s^r.$$
Write $\iota_s^r$ for the degree-$r$ coprojections. The comparison identifies the target coprojection with $j_!\iota_s^r$, and functoriality gives $(j_!d^r)(j_!\iota_s^r)=(j_!\iota_s^{r+1})(j_!d_s^r)$. Equality on every coprojection proves compatibility with the differentials. Thus the comparisons give an isomorphism of complexes and hence $J(\bigoplus_sK_s)\cong\bigoplus_sJ(K_s)$ in the derived category. For $I=\varnothing$, both coproduct complexes are zero and the exact additive $j_!$ sends zero to zero, so this comparison is also invertible. No boundedness or constructibility assumption is imposed on this family.

proof.text: Let $K\in\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$. By [sk-def-sfb-constructible] it is bounded constructible in the module-object sense. Apply [lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves] to $j$ and $\Lambda$. Its scheme hypothesis is exactly our standing separated finite-type setting, and it allows every commutative condensed ring, hence each of the admissible rings here. It concludes that the same levelwise object $JK$ is bounded constructible on $X$. Thus this use is the extension-by-zero preservation theorem already available in the restricted-functor package, with no passage to a different coefficient category.

proof.text:
Choose a Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $K$, meaning that $H^r(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_U}N)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ for every module sheaf $N$ on $U$, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $M$ be any module sheaf on $X$, placed in degree zero. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], $j^*$ is the exact inverse image, so its derived functor sends $M[0]$ to $(j^*M)[0]$. Specialize [det-lem-int-tensor-projection] to the locally closed immersion with open part $u=j$ and closed part $i=\operatorname{id}_X$ (thus $\overline S=X$). The identity direct and inverse images are identity functors, giving
$$(JK)\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}M\cong j_!(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_U}j^*M).$$
The Tor hypothesis applies to the sheaf $j^*M$. The exactness calculation in step 1 therefore identifies the degree $r$ cohomology on the right with $j_!H^r(K\otimes^L j^*M)$, which is zero outside $[a,b]$. Since $M$ was arbitrary, this is precisely finite Tor amplitude for $JK$. Together with step 3 it gives $JK\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. This uniform calculation covers finite, integral and field coefficients, and requires neither a geometric-stalk conservativity assertion nor an equality $\Dctf=\Dbc$ at an integral stage.

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-image-localizing-principle] with $\mathcal T=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})$, $\mathcal T'=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, $F=J$, $\mathcal G=\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal G'=\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. The ambient categories have all small direct sums by step 2; $J$ is triangulated by step 1 and preserves those sums by step 2. Step 4 gives $J(\mathcal G)\subseteq\mathcal G'\subseteq\Loc(\mathcal G')$, where the second inclusion is part of the definition [sk-def-localizing-closure]. All hypotheses of the cited principle hold. Its conclusion gives the required restricted functor and says that it is exact and preserves direct sums; these are the ambient sums, since both localizing closures are full triangulated subcategories closed under them.
